title: Permission census expansion by rite, jurisdiction and period, with regional-variants gap work: batch 4, 2026-10-21
semantics: Continuation register to regional-mission-permissions-2026-10-20 (49 findings, unchanged). Each finding keeps apart the approval or permission event (authority, date, territory or people), the component extent and any evidenced actual use. A permission, reprint, translation confirmation or use regime never by itself manufactures a new textual state, rite, ancestry or universal adoption. Eastern findings are recorded here only; Eastern dossiers belong to other lanes.

evidence_basis_vocabulary.original-instrument: The instrument's own text read in its official publication (AAS, ASS, full decree printed in Notitiae, official vatican.va text).
evidence_basis_vocabulary.official-journal-report: A dated decree summary or register entry with protocol number in the issuing body's own journal or yearbook (Notitiae Summarium decretorum, SICO approvals list).
evidence_basis_vocabulary.official-retrospective: A later official or Church-institutional account of the event (later decree recital, Dicastery web list, commission note, official news service).
evidence_basis_vocabulary.reproduced-instrument: The instrument's text read only as reproduced (or translated) by a third party.

review_files.storage: Untracked scratch packets pinned by SHA-256; findings repeat public source URL and locus.

independent_review.reviewer: independent batch-4 cold reviewer, distinct from the lane author and the coordinator
independent_review.scope: The reviewer fetched the cited official publications into its own scratch and re-read every one of the 70 new findings at its cited locus: AAS/ASS OCR volumes and monthly AAS issues, Notitiae scans and text layers, SICO, the Eastern Congregation list, the Syro-Malabar commission note, the Maronite, Chaldean, Vatican News, blog and bulletin pages. Authority, date, protocol, scope, component extent, basis label and actual-use wording were checked. Also checked: the documented Lyon 1902 approval stage, the evidence appended to the lyon1866, poland1986 and zaire1988 stages, the five gap dispositions, the four new Western source rows, the three owned route rows, duplication against the 49 existing findings and other receipts, ownership and tracked-file hygiene. Corrections: Lyon 1902 blessings are added 'prout in usu' and do not show a state distinct from 1866; the Ge'ez finding was relabelled official-retrospective and its unsourced 2024 and 1945 details were removed; 'page image' claims on vatican.va OCR volumes were qualified; the inferred 1 December 2019 date was qualified; the zaire gap disposition was set to unchanged-searched; supersessions were added; several loci, dates, use wording and cross-receipt relations were fixed. Not independently checked: Numelyo views 5-10 (re-fetch refused; view 8 was checked on the lane's hash-verified bytes), the Francis letter of 3 July 2021, the 519 MB Chaldean book, most non-admissions, and the searches, which were not re-run.

permissions.authority: Congregation for Divine Worship by mandate of John Paul II; letter to presidents of episcopal conferences, signed A. Mayer (pro-prefect) and V. Noè, Prot. 686/84
permissions.scope: Diocesan bishops may grant the indult to priests and faithful explicitly named in a petition to them; churches and oratories the bishop designates, not parish churches except by extraordinary concession
permissions.book_or_component: Use of the Missale Romanum according to the 1962 typical edition, in Latin, without mixing rites or texts of the two Missals; no new book or text
permissions.established: A dated papal indult, delegated to diocesan bishops, permitting celebration from an existing typical edition under five conditions (a–e); under (e) each bishop reports his concessions to the Congregation and, after one year, the outcome.
permissions.limit: A use permission, not a new textual state; does not identify which printings were used, which dioceses granted it, or any dated celebration. Superseded: Summorum Pontificum art. 1 (AAS 99 (2007) 779) replaces the conditions set by Quattuor abhinc annos and Ecclesia Dei.
permissions.locus: AAS 76 (1984), printed pp. 1088–1089 (PDF pp. 1088–1089), Epistula 'De usu Missalis Romani iuxta editionem typicam anni MCMLXII'
permissions.actual_use_state: Permission regime only; no grant or celebration evidenced here.
permissions.inspection: Text layer read for both pages; PDF p. 1088 page image viewed. Cold review: the vatican.va OCR volume is a text rendering with no page facsimiles, so a viewed page shows the OCR text, not a scan of the printed page.

permissions.authority: John Paul II, apostolic letter motu proprio Ecclesia Dei
permissions.scope: Whole Latin Church; establishes a commission for those formerly linked to the Society of St Pius X
permissions.book_or_component: Use of the Missale Romanum, 1962 typical edition; no new book
permissions.established: n. 6(a) erects the commission; n. 6(c) asks for 'amplam ac liberalem applicationem' of norms already issued on the 1962 Missal (footnote cites Quattuor abhinc annos).
permissions.limit: Does not itself alter the 1984 conditions or approve any text; implementation is left to bishops. Superseded as to conditions: Summorum Pontificum art. 1 (2007) replaces the conditions set by Quattuor abhinc annos and Ecclesia Dei.
permissions.locus: AAS 80 (1988), printed pp. 1495–1498 (PDF pp. 1495–1498), n. 6(a)–(c) and n. 9 footnote on p. 1498
permissions.actual_use_state: Permission regime only; no dated celebration evidenced here.
permissions.inspection: Text layer of pp. 1495–1498 read.

permissions.authority: Benedict XVI, apostolic letter motu proprio Summorum Pontificum
permissions.date: 2007-07-07 signed; 2007-09-14 effective
permissions.scope: Latin-rite Church: any Latin priest without people (art. 2); communities of consecrated life (art. 3); stable groups in parishes via the parish priest (art. 5); bishop and Ecclesia Dei commission recourse (arts. 7–8, 11–12)
permissions.book_or_component: 1962 typical edition of the Missale Romanum as 'extraordinary expression' of the Roman lex orandi (art. 1); readings may be in the vernacular using Apostolic See-recognized editions (art. 6); older Rituale, Pontificale (Confirmation) and Breviary also covered (art. 9)
permissions.established: Replaces the 1984 and 1988 conditions; declares the 1962 Missal never abrogated; permits celebration from it under the stated articles, effective 14 September 2007.
permissions.limit: A use regime over an existing typical edition, not a new book or textual state; vernacular-reading permission concerns readings only. Superseded in its operative norms by Traditionis custodes (2021).
permissions.locus: AAS 99 (2007), printed pp. 777–781; September 2007 issue PDF pp. 9–13; arts. 1–2 on printed p. 779 (PDF p. 11), effective-date clause p. 781
permissions.actual_use_state: Permission regime only; local celebrations not evidenced in this receipt.
permissions.inspection: Text layer of printed pp. 777–781 read; PDF p. 11 page image viewed.

permissions.authority: Pontifical Commission Ecclesia Dei, instruction, ratified by Benedict XVI in audience of 8 April 2011; signed Card. W. Levada, G. Pozzo
permissions.scope: Whole Latin Church; implements Summorum Pontificum
permissions.book_or_component: Liturgical books of the extraordinary form to be used 'ut prostant' (n. 24); new saints and some new prefaces may and should be inserted in the old Missal as later determined (n. 25); 1962 readings may be read in Latin, Latin then vernacular, or vernacular only at low Mass (n. 26)
permissions.established: Defines stable groups, priest suitability and the commission's competence; announces, without itself supplying, future additions of saints and prefaces to the 1962 Missal.
permissions.limit: Announces component additions but approves no new text; the prefaces and saints were approved only in 2020 (see cdf-quo-magis-2020, cdf-cum-sanctissima-2020). Traditionis custodes art. 8 (AAS 113 (2021) 796) abrogates earlier norms, concessions and customs that do not conform to it; the instruction is superseded to that extent.
permissions.locus: AAS 103 (2011), printed pp. 413–420; June 2011 issue PDF pp. 47–54; nn. 24–26 printed pp. 418–419; date and signatures p. 420
permissions.actual_use_state: Permission regime only.
permissions.inspection: Text layer read for the instruction, nn. 1–35 and closing formula.

permissions.authority: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith (successor to the Ecclesia Dei commission), decree Quo magis, ratified by Francis in audience of 5 December 2019; signed Card. L. Ladaria, Abp G. Morandi

permissions.established: Approves and concedes seven preface texts with rubrics of use, effective 19 March 2020; a concrete component addition to the extraordinary-form Missal, not a new edition.
permissions.limit: Optional additions attached to an existing typical edition; no new typical edition is declared. Their continued use after Traditionis custodes depends on the 2021 regime (TC art. 3 §3 footnote cites both 2020 decrees).
permissions.locus: AAS 112 (2020), printed pp. 374–380 (April 2020 issue PDF pp. 24–30); effective-date and audience clauses printed p. 375
permissions.actual_use_state: Approval and effectiveness established; actual use of individual prefaces not evidenced.
permissions.inspection: Text layer read for decree and annex headings.

permissions.authority: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, decree Cum sanctissima, ratified by Francis; signed Card. L. Ladaria, Abp G. Morandi
permissions.date: 2020-02-22 signed; 2020-03-19 effective
permissions.scope: Celebrations under the 1962 Missal; existing particular calendar concessions preserved

permissions.authority: Francis, apostolic letter motu proprio Traditionis custodes
permissions.date: 2021-07-16 signed and effective on publication in L'Osservatore Romano
permissions.scope: Diocesan bishops in the Latin Church; groups already celebrating with the pre-1970 Missal; priests ordained before and after the motu proprio; institutes formerly under Ecclesia Dei
permissions.book_or_component: Use of the 1962 Missale Romanum; books promulgated by Paul VI and John Paul II declared the unique expression of the Roman lex orandi (art. 1); readings in vernacular using conference-approved translations (art. 3 §3)

permissions.locus: AAS 113 (2021), printed pp. 793–796; August 2021 issue PDF pp. 1–4; arts. 1–8 printed pp. 794–796
permissions.actual_use_state: Permission regime only; diocesan implementation not evidenced here.
permissions.inspection: Text layer of the complete motu proprio read.

permissions.authority: Congregation for Bishops (Congregatio pro Episcopis) by special papal mandate, decree Animarum bonum, Card. G. B. Re, Prot. 1026/2001
permissions.scope: Personal Apostolic Administration of St John Mary Vianney, coextensive with the diocese of Campos, Brazil; enrolled clergy and lay members
permissions.book_or_component: Eucharist, sacraments, Liturgy of the Hours and other rites 'secundum Ritum Romanum ac disciplinam liturgicam' as ordered by Pius V with adaptations up to John XXIII (art. III) — i.e. the pre-1970 books, unnamed by edition

permissions.actual_use_state: Jurisdictional faculty established; dated celebrations not evidenced here.

permissions.authority: Benedict XVI, apostolic constitution Anglicanorum coetibus
permissions.scope: Personal ordinariates for former Anglicans erected by the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith
permissions.book_or_component: Liturgical books 'Anglicanae traditioni peculiares, ab Apostolica Sede adprobatos' for Eucharist, sacraments and Hours, alongside Roman Rite celebrations (art. III)
permissions.established: The enabling instrument that permits ordinariates to celebrate from Holy See-approved Anglican-tradition books; prerequisite for the 2015 Divine Worship approval.
permissions.limit: Grants a faculty conditional on later approval of specific books; approves no text itself. The 2015 missal approval instrument remains uninspected (see regional-variants:divineworship-gap).
permissions.locus: AAS 101 (2009), printed pp. 985–990; December 2009 issue PDF pp. 1–6; art. III printed p. 987 (PDF p. 3)

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites, letters to the bishops of the provinces of Gorizia, Zara and Zagreb, approved by Leo XIII after a special cardinals' congregation; signed Card. C. Mazzella, D. Panici
permissions.scope: Churches in the Gorizia, Zara and Zagreb provinces that can prove at least thirty years' continuous Old Slavonic use; to be listed by each bishop
permissions.book_or_component: Mass and Office in Old Church Slavonic from glagolitic-printed books recognized by the Apostolic See; people's responses in Slavonic, with Latin-script manuals for the faithful; Slavonic Rituale if approved; Epistle and Gospel sung in Slavonic after Latin where customary
permissions.established: Treats the Slavonic usage as a real (church-attached) privilege, recites earlier concessions (Innocent IV to Senj 1248 and Veglia 1252; Urban VIII's 1631 glagolitic books; Benedict XIV's 1754 edition; Pius VI's 1791 Breviary; SRC 13 February 1892) and sets fourteen rules.
permissions.limit: The 1248/1252/1631/1754 concessions are recited, not inspected in their original instruments. The privileged-church catalogue itself is not inspected; no specific Missal printing is identified.
permissions.locus: Acta Sanctae Sedis 31 (1898–99), printed pp. 310–313 (PDF pp. 310–313), rules I–XIV and date clause p. 313
permissions.actual_use_state: Existing use presupposed by the privilege test; no church-by-church use evidenced here.
permissions.inspection: Text layer of printed pp. 310–313 read (spaced OCR).

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites, decree De usu linguae Slavonicae in sacra Liturgia, by mandate of Pius X; signed Card. S. Cretoni, D. Panici
permissions.scope: Dioceses of the Gorizia, Zara and Zagreb provinces; only churches with proven uninterrupted glagolitic use from 1868 onward
permissions.book_or_component: Same book requirement as 1898 (glagolitic characters, Apostolic See approval); suspension ipso facto for unauthorized introduction; Epistle/Gospel-only Slavonic and Croatian vernacular singing excluded from the privilege
permissions.established: Re-promulgates the 1898 rules with changes: catalogue due by July of the next year, 1868 baseline, penalties, and stricter rules for priests moving between Latin and Slavonic churches.
permissions.limit: Regulates permission scope; identifies no printing; the resulting catalogue is not inspected.
permissions.locus: Acta Sanctae Sedis 40 (1907), printed pp. 54–58 (PDF pp. 54–58); date clause p. 58
permissions.actual_use_state: Use presupposed for privileged churches; none individually evidenced here.
permissions.inspection: Text layer of printed pp. 54–58 read.

permissions.authority: Pius XI through the Sacred Congregation of Rites (Zagrabien. et aliarum), signed Card. A. Vico, A. Mariani

permissions.book_or_component: New edition of the Missale Romano-Slavonicum printed in Latin characters, prepared by Josef Vajs and revised by Abp A. Bauer and Bp J. Mileta
permissions.established: Approval and indult for a Latin-script edition of the Romano-Slavonic Missal, departing from the 1898/1906 requirement that books be printed in glagolitic characters.
permissions.limit: The decree concerns script and approval; it does not describe textual differences from earlier glagolitic editions. Candidate and source already exist in the Western inventory (roman-adaptations-src-aas1927); this finding adds only the permission record.
permissions.locus: AAS 19 (1927), printed p. 156 (PDF p. 156), decree VII
permissions.actual_use_state: Approval for lawful Slavonic users; dated use of the printed edition not evidenced here.
permissions.inspection: Text layer of printed p. 156 read.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation for the Sacraments and Divine Worship, decreta generalia, Prot. CD 151/84
permissions.scope: Dioceses of Poland
permissions.book_or_component: Polish text of the Missale Romanum (whole Missal translation)

permissions.limit: Strengthens the 1984 element of the existing poland-1986 finding without replacing it; regional components (calendar, Holy Week, prefaces) and the 1983 bishops' approval are not itemized in the summary. No printing date.

permissions.inspection: Text layer and PDF p. 13 page image viewed.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation for the Sacraments and Divine Worship, decreta generalia, Prot. CD 1726/84 and CD 1727/84
permissions.scope: Dioceses of Poland
permissions.book_or_component: Polish translation of the Eucharistic Prayers for Masses of Reconciliation (CD 1726/84); concession of the Swiss synod Eucharistic Prayer, granted to Switzerland on 8 August 1974 (Prot. CD 1972/74), for use in Polish dioceses (CD 1727/84)
permissions.established: Two dated anaphora permissions for Poland, the second extending a regional Eucharistic Prayer from one territory to another.
permissions.limit: Summary entries; the Polish text of the Swiss prayer and its variants are not inspected here. The 1974 Swiss grant is cited from this summary, not from its own instrument.
permissions.locus: Notitiae 20 (1984), n. 221, Summarium decretorum, printed p. 947 (PDF p. 33), 'Polonia'
permissions.actual_use_state: Permission only; the 1986 Missal's inclusion of these prayers is described in the existing poland-1986 finding.
permissions.inspection: Text layer and PDF p. 33 page image viewed.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites (ordinary session of 22 April 1902, relator Card. V. Vannutelli), ratified and indulted by Leo XIII; signed Card. D. Ferrata, D. Panici
permissions.scope: Whole clergy of the archdiocese of Lyon, on petition of Card. P.-H. Coullié with the metropolitan chapter
permissions.book_or_component: New edition titled 'Missale Romanum, in quo antiqui ritus Lugdunenses servantur, Apostolicae Sedis auctoritate recognitum et probatum', with particular rubrics, liturgical texts and saints' Masses; adds, 'prout in usu' (as customary), two blessings in solemn Mass (new fruits on St James, grapes on the Transfiguration)
permissions.established: Approves a new Roman-based Lyon missal edition and its title. The narrative also records that Card. de Bonald, following Pius IX, introduced the Roman Missal and Breviary and obtained Apostolic approval of a Lyon calendar and proper of Offices and Masses, retaining some cleansed Lyon rites.
permissions.limit: The narrative gives no date for the Bonald-era approval, so it does not verify the reported 17 March 1864 brief. The approved exemplar and its printing year are not inspected; the decree does not enumerate retained rites beyond the two added blessings. Because the two blessings are added 'prout in usu', they are not evidence of a change from earlier Lyon practice or from the 1866 book. The narrative also calls the Bonald-era project to print the Roman Missal under the granted privileges 'vix inceptum' (barely begun); how that relates to the 1866 printing is unresolved.
permissions.locus: Acta Sanctae Sedis 35 (1902–03), printed pp. 614–616 (PDF pp. 614–616), 'Lugdunen.'; title, blessings and date on p. 616
permissions.actual_use_state: Indult for use by the whole Lyon clergy; first printing and dated use not evidenced.
permissions.inspection: Text layer of pp. 614–616 read; PDF p. 616 page image viewed. Cold review: the vatican.va OCR volume is a text rendering with no page facsimiles, so a viewed page shows the OCR text, not a scan of the printed page.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship, decreta generalia, Prot. n. 1256/74
permissions.scope: Yugoslavia (episcopal conference territory)
permissions.book_or_component: Old Church Slavonic ('paleoslavica') translation of the Order of Mass and Eucharistic Prayers of the Missale Romanum
permissions.established: A dated Roman confirmation extending the historical Slavonic liturgical language to the postconciliar Order of Mass and Eucharistic Prayers.
permissions.limit: Summary entry only; the confirmed text, its script and any printed edition are not inspected. Whether use remained limited to the historically privileged churches is not stated.
permissions.locus: Notitiae 10 (1974), nn. 95–96, Acta Congregationis, printed p. 237 (PDF p. 19), 'Iugoslavia'
permissions.actual_use_state: Confirmation only; no dated celebration evidenced.
permissions.inspection: Text layer and PDF p. 19 page image viewed (file acquired by sub-lane B).

permissions.authority: John Paul II, address to bishops of Zaire on their ad limina visit
permissions.scope: Dioceses of Zaire
permissions.book_or_component: Eucharistic celebration form then in use ad experimentum, to be examined further by the dicasteries before entering 'un missel à l'usage des diocèses du Zaïre'; wider ritual of sacraments in view
permissions.established: Contemporary papal text records that one week before the 30 April 1988 decree the Zairean Mass form was still experimental and not yet in a missal.
permissions.limit: An address, not an act; it does not contradict or date the decree, and gives no printing or effective date. The two texts are kept separate without harmonization. The evidence_basis label records that the original address text was read in AAS; an address is not a permission instrument (rule address-is-not-act).
permissions.locus: AAS 80 (1988), printed pp. 1449–1453, address VIII dated 23 April 1988; the ad experimentum sentence printed p. 1452 (PDF p. 1452)
permissions.actual_use_state: Experimental use of the form presupposed by the address; individual celebrations not identified.
permissions.inspection: Text layer read; PDF p. 1452 page image viewed. Cold review: the vatican.va OCR volume is a text rendering with no page facsimiles, so a viewed page shows the OCR text, not a scan of the printed page.

permissions.authority: Georges Darboy, archbishop of Paris, 'Licentia et approbatio Ordinarii', countersigned E. J. Lagarde
permissions.scope: Printers Adrien Le Clere et Soc., Paris; the licence is for their Missale Romanum, here bound as the base of the 1866 Missale romano-lugdunense
permissions.book_or_component: Missale Romanum according to the Roman edition of 1861, with additional Masses for the general calendar and Masses 'pro aliquibus locis legitime indultas'; printing licence and conformity attestation
permissions.established: Original licence printed in the Lyon 1866 book: the Paris ordinary licensed and approved Le Clere's Roman Missal after collation with the authentic Roman originals.
permissions.limit: A printing and conformity licence, not a Lyon permission; it is the only 1864 instrument in the inspected front matter (views 5–10) and does not verify the reported 17 March 1864 papal brief.
permissions.locus: Missale romano-lugdunense (Paris: Le Clere, 1866), Bibliothèque municipale de Lyon copy, Numelyo view 8
permissions.actual_use_state: Printing licence only.
permissions.inspection: Page image of Numelyo view 8 viewed (with views 5, 6, 9 and 10 for context).
permissions.relation_to_existing_register: Adds front-matter evidence to existing finding lyon-1866; it does not verify that finding's title claim of Apostolic See authority.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation for the Eastern Church, Cardinal Eugène Tisserant (secretary) and Archbishop Antonino Arata (assessor), Circular I, prot. 1219/28; implementing the plenary session of 10 January 1938 approved by Pius XI on 15 January 1938
permissions.date: 1941-09-10 circular; 1938-01-10 plenary decision and 1938-01-15 papal approval recited
permissions.scope: Ukrainian (Ruthenian) ordinaries; seminaries, scholasticates and religious novitiates of their jurisdictions; clergy under Latin ordinaries reserved to the Congregation
permissions.book_or_component: Church Slavonic Ruthenian-recension books printed by the Congregation: a small-format extract of the Liturgikon/Sluzhebnik (Vespers, Matins, hours) and the Chrysostom Liturgy in larger and smaller formats; the complete Liturgikon still in press; rubric component expressly restored against post-1692/1733 Latinizing rubrics
permissions.established: The circular sends three copies of each printed book, states the restoration principle (oldest Ruthenian recension, Benedict XIV's 1754 Greek text as rubrical guide), forbids changing Zamość-based practice without Holy See permission, lets ordinaries dispense where Zamość observance is recent custom, asks that Zamość/Lviv rules not be introduced elsewhere, lets priests ordained before the circular celebrate privately in the old manner, and orders seminaries, scholasticates and novitiates to celebrate henceforth by the new Liturgikon.
permissions.limit: Read only in the contemporary Ukrainian translation sent from Rome, as reproduced on a blog; the signed Italian original and its archival copy are not inspected. The circular does not itself date the 1942 complete Liturgikon, the 1944 Ordo celebrationis or any eparchy's adoption. Formats are not separate textual states. Bounded searches of AAS 33 (1941) and 34 (1942) found no publication of this circular.
permissions.locus: Blog reproduction (Liturgiia Tserkvy, October 2016) of Circular I, Rome 10 September 1941, prot. 1219/28: opening paragraph (books sent; 1938 plenary and papal approval), principles 1-6, norms 1-5, signatures

gap_dispositions.evidence: 1866 front matter views 5–10 read (Paris archiepiscopal printing licence of 13 January 1864; no Lyon brief there); SRC decree of 1 May 1902 records the undated Bonald-era Apostolic approval of the Lyon calendar and proper and approves a new edition. New gap regional-variants:lyon-1902-gap added for the 1902 edition.
gap_dispositions.remaining: The 1864 brief itself, Lyon-specific front matter beyond view 10, and text comparison with 1825/1844.

gap_dispositions.evidence: Notitiae 20 (1984) decree summaries: Prot. CD 151/84 (28 April 1984) confirms the Polish Missal; CD 1726/84 and 1727/84 (21 November 1984) Polish Reconciliation prayers and the Swiss synod prayer for Poland.
gap_dispositions.remaining: Full 1983/1984 instruments, original book leaves, 2009/2010 and 2013 approvals and contents.

gap_dispositions.evidence: AAS 80 (1988) 1452: papal address of 23 April 1988 calls the form ad experimentum, not yet in a missal; papal video message of 1 December 2020 attests a 2019 Congolese-Rite Mass in St Peter's. Cold review: neither item resolves a listed missing element (bound approved missal, complete calendar and propers, first printing, effectiveness, later revisions); they add pre-approval status and later use context, so the disposition is unchanged-searched rather than narrowed.
gap_dispositions.remaining: Bound approved missal, first printing and diocesan rollout.

gap_dispositions.evidence: Metropolitan Cantor Institute service-book directory listed and checked; no 2007 clergy Liturgikon online; the Slavonic Complete PDF is a private-use parish compilation (non-admission).
gap_dispositions.remaining: Two 2007 clergy Liturgikons, earlier English streams and collation.

gap_dispositions.evidence: Anglicanorum coetibus art. III (AAS 101 (2009) 987) read as the enabling instrument; no 2015 approval decree found in Notitiae 51 (2015), web searches or ordinariate.net (HTTP 403); secondary reports of a 27 May 2015 decree unverified.
gap_dispositions.remaining: Signed 2015 decree, complete printed missal, 2003 Book of Divine Worship collation and later updates.

remaining_gaps: Original instruments still missing for: Lyon 1864 brief; Divine Worship 2015 decree; Polish 1983 bishops' act and 2009/2010/2013 approvals; Chinese 1615 brief and 1949 indult; England-and-Wales 1971 indult; Ruthenian 1941 circular in its original language.

Notitiae years not harvested for order or diocesan propers: 1965–68, 1970, 1977–80, 1983–87, 1989–2002, 2004–07, 2009–11, 2013–22; image-only issues 077 (1972), 080 and 082 (1973), 110 (1975), 269 (1988) not OCR'd.
Eastern: definitive Chaldean recognitio after 2014, Ge'ez 2024 recognitio decree, Syro-Malankara approvals beyond the register, Ethiopian 1945 Rome missal approval leaf.
Actual-use evidence remains thin: most findings establish approval only.
Cameroon, Papua New Guinea and other SC 37–40 / Varietates legitimae adaptation instruments not searched.
limits: A bounded expansion, not an exhaustive census. 70 new findings across Roman, Slavonic-Roman, Lyon, Polish, Zaire, order, diocesan, inculturated and Eastern settings, 1898–2025 in instruments (with earlier concessions recited). Evidence bases are recorded per finding; official-journal decree summaries are contemporary official records but not full decrees. No new candidate, transition or Eastern dossier edit is made; one documented Lyon approval stage is added. Sub-lane packets were reviewed by the lane coordinator with spot checks (AAS 78 (1986) 588–589; Notitiae 11 (1975) 45; Notitiae 10 (1974) 237), not by an independent cold reviewer.
